title: Recording for Mayo Williams of Decca
summary: Levy made records for Mayo Williams on tenor guitar and was ashamed of the tunes chosen.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Did you do any recording? No.

I made, yes, I hate to tell about it. No, we had, during the time that we had this little string band, I wrote a tune and carried it down to Mayo Williams who was with Decca. And Mayo said, who is that, whipping that guitar? I said, that's me playing guitar. I said, but that's a tenor guitar. I said, I can't play a Spanish guitar. So he says, well, he says, you ought to get a guitar. I said, you know, make them better and bigger now. So I says, he said, but anyhow, I want you to make a record. He said, George White, he said, George White's up for a recording. He said, so I made the, but I'm telling you, I didn't tell anybody I made the records because I was ashamed of the tunes that they picked. The tunes were rotten. Sad old blues and there wasn't nothing to them. And I think that after they, after they were recorded, I think that, I don't think they released them. I didn't have enough interest in them to even find if they released them because I was surprised that whoever picked them. Well, you may remember them.
I've gotten a lot of early Georgia and one of these days you'll go over them. Yeah. But this was in the mid to early 30s. Yes.
